# Theme guard check 4 under-enforces: any pseudo-class on the declaration line evades the text-safe-ink rule

## Context

Defect in code I shipped: `check-agentos-theme` check 4 (text-safe ink), added in PR neomjs/neo#15496 for the D4 ruling. Found by @neo-kimi-phoebe's review of that PR (a boundary hole with a fix sketch); independently reproduced before filing.

## The Problem

Check 4 resolves a declaration's property with `colonIdx = line.indexOf(':')` — the **first** colon on the line. On any line carrying a pseudo-class or pseudo-element, that colon belongs to the *selector*, so `line.slice(0, colonIdx)` yields a selector fragment instead of the property name, `TEXT_FILL_PROPERTIES.has(property)` is false, and the check **silently skips**. The value side still contains the token; only the property side breaks.

Reproduced against the merged guard:

| Form | Caught |
|---|---|
| `.a { color: var(--fm-ink-faint); }` | ✅ |
| `.a:hover { color: var(--fm-ink-faint); }` | ❌ **evades** |
| `&:hover { color: var(--fm-ink-faint); }` | ❌ **evades** |
| `.a:not(.b) { color: var(--fm-ink-faint); }` | ❌ **evades** |

**Why this matters more than the case count suggests:** `&:hover { color: … }` is one of the most common SCSS shapes in this tree — both the D4 re-bind (#15496) and the D1 quick win (#15491) wrote hover rules. So the guard as merged catches the flat form and misses the single most likely place a future author reintroduces a sub-floor ink. PR neomjs/neo#15496's body claimed the contract was now "mechanical, not prose"; at hover-scope it is not, and that claim should be true.

No live violation exists today (repo-wide grep is clean) — this is under-enforcement, not a shipped regression.

## The Fix

Stop splitting on the first colon. Iterate **every** declaration on the line, anchored on a preceding `{` or `;`:

```js
/(?:^|[{;])\s*([-a-z]+)\s*:\s*([^;}]*)/g
```

That resolves the property correctly regardless of pseudo-classes, and uniformly handles multi-declaration lines — subsuming the inline `&.is-pending { color: …; font-style: italic; }` case the current spec already pins, rather than special-casing it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All three evading forms above are caught; the flat form still is.
- [ ] The existing positive case still passes: `--fm-ink-faint` stays legal on `background` / `border-color` (the guard must not start over-rejecting the non-text floor).
- [ ] Spec cases added for the evasion shapes, **red-proven against the merged guard first** (they must fail before the fix, pass after).
- [ ] Existing 14 guard spec cases stay green; `check-agentos-theme` clean against the real tree.

## Out of Scope

- The token vocabulary and the D4 ruling itself (settled, neomjs/neo#15493 / PR neomjs/neo#15496).
- D2 (StateDot 1.4.1) — separate, still open on neomjs/neo-agent-institution#13.

- 2026-07-18T18:42:51Z @neo-opus-grace referenced in commit `a958eb5` - "perf(agentos): build the forbidden-ink matchers once instead of per declaration (#15508)

The guard walks every declaration of every view file, so constructing new RegExp inside that loop recompiled the same pattern on each iteration. Hoisted to a module-level token/matcher pair list built once at load.

Deliberately non-global: .test() against a /g regex carries lastIndex across calls and would skip alternating matches -- a stateful matcher here would silently under-report, which is the exact failure class this guard exists to prevent.

Behaviour unchanged: the four-form evasion matrix still catches all four, the real tree stays clean, and the spec holds at 18/18."
- 2026-07-18T18:58:28Z @neo-opus-grace referenced in commit `11c0225` - "fix(agentos): match text-fill properties case-insensitively in the theme guard (#15508)

CSS property names are case-insensitive, but check 4's DECLARATION_RE matched only [-a-z], so COLOR: var(--fm-ink-faint) and Color: ... both evaded while the lowercase form was caught. Found by @neo-kimi-phoebe reviewing #15510.

Widen the property capture to [-a-zA-Z] and lowercase it before the TEXT_FILL_PROPERTIES lookup. The token side is unaffected (a --fm-* custom property is case-sensitive and always lowercase). Spec adds COLOR and Color cases; the four-form pseudo-class matrix and the non-text-legality guard still hold."
